{{Short description|British mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Graham Robert Everest''' (14 December 1957 in [[Southwick, West Sussex]] – 30 July 2010) was a British mathematician working on [[arithmetic dynamics]] and [[Recurrence relation|recursive equations]] in [[number theory]].

==Life==
Everest studied at Bedford College (now [[Royal Holloway College]]) of the [[University of London]] where he completed a Ph.D. in 1983 under the supervision of [[Colin J. Bushnell]] of [[King's College London]] (''The distribution of normal integral generators in tame extensions of Q.'')<ref>[http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=15051 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref>  He joined the faculty of the [[University of East Anglia]] in 1983 as a lecturer and spent his academic career there.

He was ordained a priest in the [[Church of England]] in 2006. He died of prostate cancer on 30 July 2010, leaving behind his wife and three children.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://newsletter.lms.ac.uk/396/396_09.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015010738/http://newsletter.lms.ac.uk/396/396_09.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 October 2012 |journal=Newsletter of the London Mathematical Society |number=396 |date=14 September 2010 |author=Thomas Ward |title=Deaths: Graham Everest |accessdate=2014-02-23 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Ward | first=Thomas | year=2013 | title=Obituary: Graham Everest 1957–2010 | journal=[[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] | volume=45 | number=5 | pages=1110–1118 | doi=10.1112/blms/bdt053| s2cid=117006730 | url=http://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/108998/1/1306.0131.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Everest|first=James|date=2010-11-03|title=Graham Everest obituary|language=en-GB|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/theguardian/2010/nov/03/graham-everest-obituary|access-date=2020-07-04|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 1983 he became a member of the [[London Mathematical Society]]. In 2012 he was awarded the [[Lester Randolph Ford Award]] jointly with [[Thomas Ward (mathematician)|Thomas Ward]] for their work in [[diophantine equation]]s.<ref>American Mathematical Monthly, Volume 118, 2011, pp. 594–598, [http://maa.org/news/MathFest2012awards/Ford.html MAA Ford Award 2012] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140227173638/http://www.maa.org/news/MathFest2012awards/Ford.html |date=27 February 2014 }}</ref>

== Writing ==
* With [[Thomas Ward (Mathematician)|Thomas Ward]]: ''[https://www.springer.com/gb/book/9781852339173 Introduction to Number Theory]'', [[Springer-Verlag]]  2005.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Everest, Graham, 1957-|title=An introduction to number theory|date=2005|publisher=Springer|others=Ward, Thomas, 1963-|isbn=1-85233-917-9|location=London|oclc=57201073}}</ref>
* With [[Alf van der Poorten]], [[Thomas Ward (Mathematician)|Thomas Ward]], and [[Igor Shparlinski]]: ''[https://bookstore.ams.org/surv-104 Recurrence sequences]'', [[American Mathematical Society]] 2003.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Recurrence sequences|date=2003|publisher=American Mathematical Society|others=Everest, Graham, 1957-|isbn=0-8218-3387-1|location=Providence, RI|oclc=52165737}}</ref>
* With [[Thomas Ward (Mathematician)|Thomas Ward]]: ''[https://www.springer.com/gb/book/9781852331252 Heights of polynomials and entropy in algebraic dynamics]'', [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer Verlag]] 1999.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Everest, Graham, 1957-|title=Heights of polynomials and entropy in algebraic dynamics|date=1999|publisher=Springer|others=Ward, Thomas, 1963-|isbn=1-85233-125-9|location=London|oclc=40298416}}</ref>
